rgb: The camera wearer sits indoors in front of a small wooden table about 3.0 to 5.0 metres away and below eye level, with an open notebook and a yellow-capped pen resting on the tabletop out of arm's reach of the wearer's two visible hands. Directly ahead in the room, an empty wooden armchair with a white cloth over its backrest stands about 2.0 to 2.5 metres in front of the wearer, facing right toward a small side table with a metal cup about 0.2 metres to its right and a pink-covered bed about 1.5 to 3.0 metres away on the right side of the room. Behind the armchair and side table, a larger dark wooden desk sits against the back wall roughly 0.3 to 0.7 metres from the camera wearer and within reach, while a green wall and a curtained doorway border the left side of the room about 2.0 to 3.5 metres away. The bed on the right and the top of the near desk are partly cropped by the right and upper frame edges across all five frames, and the front edge of the wearer's table partially occludes a patterned floor mat directly beneath and behind it. In frame 3, a person wearing red clothing enters the upper-left foreground about 0.5 to 1.0 metres away and within reach, with their head cropped out of the top of the frame so their gaze is not visible, and walks rightward behind the armchair in frames 4 and 5 where their lower body is largely occluded by the chair and desk. Meanwhile, the camera wearer's viewpoint remains stationary while their right hand shifts slightly leftward across the notebook in frames 3 and 4 before returning toward the center of the page in frame 5.
depth: The monocular depth map shows the camera wearer's hands, pen, open notebook, and square tabletop in the bright background out of arm's reach at roughly 3.0 to 5.0 metres below and in front of the viewpoint, while the floor slopes darker away into the background. Beyond the table at roughly 1.8 to 3.0 metres, a bed extends along the right, an armchair angled toward the right sits in the centre-left next to a small stool about 0.2 metres to its right, and a desk sits behind the stool against the back wall at under 1 metre and within reach. In frame 3, a second person enters on the upper left at roughly 0.5 to 1.0 metres away and within reach, walking away and rightward behind the armchair in frame 4 before moving mostly behind the chair and desk in frame 5, with their upper body cropped out of the top of the frame and no face visible away from the camera wearer. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the far tabletop plane from the mid-ground furniture and reveals the continuous floor distance gradient, even where floor tiles and patterned rugs create visual clutter. However, the map is unreliable on thin or flat objects—the pen and notebook pages blend into the tabletop brightness, the walking person in frames 3 to 5 appears as a faint, blurry dark silhouette lacking sharp depth boundaries, and the dark area under the near desk loses geometric detail.
segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the background tabletop (alternately labelled 'bed' or 'dining table') at 3.0 to 5.0 metres directly in front of the camera wearer and out of arm's reach, an open 'book' resting on its left side out of arm's reach, and the camera wearer's hands ('person') overlapping and partially occluding the lower edges of the book and table. In the mid-ground around 1.8 to 3.0 metres away, it segments the 'bed' on the right and the 'chair' in the centre-left (spaced roughly 1.0 metre apart), and in frame 3 it captures the standing 'person' on the upper left about 0.5 to 1.0 metres away and within reach and 0.5 metres to the left of the chair before they walk rightward behind the chair in frames 4 and 5. Across the 5 frames, the static furniture masks remain fixed while the camera wearer's right hand mask shifts slightly left to turn a page in frames 3 and 4 and returns right in frame 5, and the foreground person appears only in frame 3 facing toward/rightward with their head cropped above the frame. This map makes object boundaries and category regions—such as the exact footprint of the open notebook and armchair—immediately distinct against patterned surfaces compared to the RGB image. However, it is unreliable in several places: it completely misses the small stool, near desk, and held pen, mislabels the wooden bed leg on the far right as a 'person' in frames 1 to 3, flickers the background table's class between 'bed' and 'dining table', drops the camera wearer's hand mask in frame 3, and fails to segment the walking person in frames 4 and 5 when partially occluded behind the chair.
pose: The pose map renders 3D-like hand skeletons (magenta) for the camera wearer's left and right hands resting on the background tabletop and notebook out of reach at 3.0 to 5.0 metres in front of and below the viewpoint, spaced roughly 0.15 to 0.25 metres apart. In frames 1 and 5, both the left hand (fingers splayed flat on the right page/table) and the right hand (curled around the pen above the left page) are tracked, showing the right hand slightly higher and to the left of the left hand. Across the sequence, the right hand opens and shifts leftward in frames 3 and 4 to lift the notebook page before returning to a writing posture in frame 5, while the foreground person walking past at 0.5 to 1.0 metres and within reach in frames 3 to 5 has no yellow body or magenta hand skeleton detected at all because their upper torso and head are out of view above the top frame edge. Compared to RGB, the pose map explicitly reveals the fine finger joint articulations and curls of the camera wearer's hands even when the pen or shadows partially obscure the fingers. It is highly unreliable across time, however, completely dropping the right hand skeleton in frame 2, missing the left hand skeleton in frames 3 and 4 despite it remaining clearly visible in the RGB frames, and failing to detect any body keypoints for the camera wearer or the walking foreground person.
